learn: Long ago, children played with wooden toys, dolls and hoops.
They played tag, marbles and hopscotch.
Many games are still played today.
check: Long-ago toys were often made of...
Which game is from long ago?
Many old games are ___ played today.
lessons.try: Play a game from long ago.

learn: Long ago, people travelled by walking, horses and wagons.
Trains and steamboats came later.
Today we have cars and planes.
lessons.try: Make a transportation timeline.

learn: Long ago, people sent letters by horse and later by train.
The telegraph and telephone came next.
Today we use phones and email.
lessons.try: Write a letter as if it's 1850.

learn: Primary sources come from the time being studied.
Letters, photos, diaries and objects are primary sources.
They help us see the past first-hand.
check: An old letter is a ___ source.
Primary sources come from the ___ being studied.
lessons.try: Look at an old photo and describe what you see.

learn: Secondary sources are made later by people studying the past.
Textbooks and encyclopedias are secondary sources.
Good historians use both kinds.
lessons.try: Compare a diary entry with a textbook page about the same event.

learn: Your family has its own history.
Grandparents and old photos tell family stories.
A family tree shows relatives over time.
check: Three generations means kids, parents and...
lessons.try: Make a family tree with three generations.

learn: Some things change, but some stay the same.
People still need food, homes, families and friends.
Children have always played and learned.
check: A Venn diagram shows what's alike and...
lessons.try: Make a Venn diagram of then and now.

learn: History studies the past using sources.
Homes, schools, toys, travel and talk have changed.
Basic needs stay the same.
check: A diary from long ago is a ___ source.
lessons.try: Make a then-and-now book.

learn: Inventors create new things that change how people live.
Benjamin Franklin experimented with electricity and invented bifocal glasses.
George Washington Carver found hundreds of uses for peanuts and helped farmers care for their soil.
check: George Washington Carver found many uses for...
lessons.try: Think of an invention that would help your family.

learn: Some people worked to make life fairer for everyone.
Harriet Tubman led enslaved people to freedom on the Underground Railroad.
Martin Luther King Jr. worked peacefully so all people would be treated equally. Rosa Parks refused to give up her bus seat and helped change unfair laws.
check: Who led people to freedom on the Underground Railroad?
How did Martin Luther King Jr. work for change?
What did Rosa Parks refuse to give up?
lessons.try: Choose one of these people and tell why they were brave.

learn: People who make a difference often see a problem and decide to help.
They are brave, keep trying and work with others.
Children can make a difference too, by helping others and speaking up for what's right.
check: People who make a difference often...
Which trait helps people make a difference?
lessons.try: Write about one way you could make a difference.

learn: Heroes help others and act with courage.
They may be famous or ordinary people.
Heroes show good character.
lessons.try: Write about someone you think is a hero.

learn: Benjamin Franklin was an inventor, writer and leader.
He experimented with electricity using a kite.
He helped start the United States.
lessons.try: Draw Franklin's kite experiment.

learn: Thomas Edison invented many things.
He made a long-lasting light bulb and the phonograph.
He failed many times but kept trying.
lessons.try: List things in your home that use electric light.

learn: Orville and Wilbur Wright built the first powered airplane.
They first flew in 1903 at Kitty Hawk.
They tested gliders for years first.
check: The Wright brothers built the first...
lessons.try: Make paper airplanes and test them.

learn: George Washington Carver was a scientist.
He found hundreds of uses for peanuts and sweet potatoes.
He helped farmers keep soil healthy.
lessons.try: List foods made from peanuts.

learn: Abraham Lincoln was the 16th President.
He grew up poor in a log cabin and loved reading.
He worked to end slavery and keep the country together.
lessons.try: Write three facts about Lincoln.

learn: Harriet Tubman escaped slavery.
She went back many times to lead others to freedom on the Underground Railroad.
She was very brave.
lessons.try: Read a short biography of Harriet Tubman.

learn: Helen Keller could not see or hear.
Her teacher, Anne Sullivan, spelled words into her hand.
Helen learned to read, write and speak, and helped others.
check: Helen Keller could not see or...
lessons.try: Try to spell a word into a partner's hand.

learn: Clara Barton was a nurse who helped wounded soldiers.
She started the American Red Cross.
The Red Cross still helps people in disasters.
lessons.try: Learn what the Red Cross does today.

learn: Sequoyah created a writing system for the Cherokee language.
Sitting Bull led the Lakota and protected his people.
Native leaders helped their nations survive and learn.
lessons.try: Learn about a Native leader from your state.

learn: Teachers, nurses, firefighters and neighbours are everyday heroes.
They help others every day.
You don't need to be famous to make a difference.
check: You need to be famous to make a difference?
lessons.try: Write a thank-you to an everyday hero.

learn: People make a difference through courage, inventions and kindness.
Inventors, leaders and helpers changed our lives.
You can make a difference too.
check: Who invented a long-lasting light bulb?
Who led people on the Underground Railroad?
Who started the American Red Cross?
lessons.try: Plan one way you'll make a difference this month.
